sections.h2: Where is Midvale, Utah, and what does the city look like on paper?
sections.html:
Midvale sits in the middle of the Salt Lake Valley, with the Jordan River as its western border and Interstate 15 running through the center. It covers about 5.9 square miles at an elevation of 4,383 feet, which makes it one of the smaller and more tightly built cities in Salt Lake County.

The Census Bureau counted 36,028 residents in 2020, up from 27,964 in 2010. That is a 28.8 percent jump in ten years, with new housing on the old smelter ground on the west side adding to it.

Fewer than half of Midvale households own their home. A seller here is often a landlord, an heir to a rental, or an owner with a tenant still living in the house.

sections.h2: How did Midvale begin, and why was it built around smelters?
sections.html:
Midvale grew from farm settlement in the 1850s into a railroad and mining service town in the 1870s, and it incorporated as a city in 1909. Its name is generally taken to reflect its central spot in the valley.

The western half became industrial because of the rail access and the link to the mines at Bingham Canyon. The eastern half stayed agricultural and then filled with housing. Fort Union, a separate early settlement on the east edge, was annexed later and brought an established neighborhood and the Shops at Fort Union into the city.

The 1910 census counted 1,760 people. By 2000 the figure was 27,029, so almost all of the city's present housing is less than a century old, and a lot of it dates from the last few decades.

sections.h2: What is Bingham Junction, and does the old slag site matter to a home seller?
sections.html:
Bingham Junction is the redeveloped 446 acres on Midvale's west side where five smelters processed lead and copper ore from 1871 to 1958. The EPA lists it as the Midvale Slag Superfund site and issued a Ready for Reuse Determination in 2008, which cleared the ground for commercial and residential use.

Today the area has a light rail station that opened in 2011, homes of several types, offices, a supermarket and a park. The EPA's December 2025 data counts 64 businesses on the site and 2,736 people employed there. Overstock's headquarters there was sold to Salt Lake County in 2024, and the EPA page says the county planned to move in during 2026.

South of it, Jordan Bluffs covers 351 acres and was part of the same slag ground. Redevelopment there is at an early stage, with proposals that could bring around 3,500 homes.

  • If your house is on the west side, a buyer or their lender may ask about the site's history, so keep any closing or cleanup paperwork you received at purchase.
  • For a specific parcel, ask the title company what it found.
  • Newer townhomes and condos near the station are sold by owners of many different loan types, which can affect how a buyer finances a nearby house.

sections.h2: Which employers, roads and train lines serve Midvale?
sections.html:
Midvale is served by two TRAX light rail lines, Interstate 15 and a short drive to Interstate 215, so most commutes in the valley are workable from here. The Census Bureau puts the average trip to work at 20.6 minutes.

  • The Red Line stops at Bingham Junction and runs to the University of Utah.
  • The Blue Line stops at Midvale Fort Union and Midvale Center.
  • 7800 South crosses the middle of the city east to west, and Main Street (700 West) runs through the historic downtown.
  • The I-15 and I-215 interchange is near 7200 South and State Street, and a ski bus runs along 7200 South.

Company headquarters listed for the city include CHG Healthcare Services, Arctic Circle Restaurants and Sportsman's Warehouse. Retail concentrates at the Shops at Fort Union on the east side and along State Street.

sections.h2: Which school district covers Midvale homes?
sections.html:
Canyons School District is the main district for Midvale. Voters approved splitting it from Jordan School District in 2007, and Canyons began operating on July 1, 2009.

Midvale has four elementary schools (Copperview, East Midvale, Midvale and Midvalley), two middle schools (Midvale Middle and Union Middle) and Hillcrest High School. Boundaries can change, so a seller who mentions schools in a listing or to a buyer should confirm the address with the district first.

sections.h2: What does Midvale's weather and ground mean for a house?
sections.html:
Midvale has a dry, four-season climate with about 14.7 inches of precipitation a year, so roofs, furnaces and air conditioners all get a real workout. The average July high is 93 degrees, the average January low is 17, and the record extremes are 110 and minus 25.

The larger risk is the ground. The Wasatch Fault runs along the valley, and the Salt Lake City segment last ruptured about 1,200 to 1,300 years ago. Experts give a 57 percent chance of a magnitude 6.0 or larger quake somewhere on the fault within 50 years. Many Wasatch Front areas sit on soft Lake Bonneville sediments, which raises liquefaction risk, and a magnitude 5.7 quake near Magna in March 2020 shook the whole valley.

For an older Midvale house, chimneys, water heater strapping and foundation cracks are the items worth looking at. Repairing or disclosing them is one of the costs a seller weighs against selling as-is.

sections.h2: What business license rules apply to Midvale landlords?
sections.html:
A landlord in Midvale needs a city landlord business license, and Midvale's published licensing page says these licenses expire August 31 and are due no later than September 15. Most other business licenses expire December 31 and are past due after January 15.

Fee amounts are adopted by the city council every year, and moving a business to a new address in the city triggers new inspections. If you are selling a rental, check that your license is current before a buyer's agent asks,.

sections.h2: How do Midvale property taxes work, and who bills them?
sections.html:
Salt Lake County values and bills Midvale property, and its published calendar runs on a single schedule for the whole county. All property is valued as it stood on January 1.

StepWhen
Assessor certifies valuesMay 22
Valuation notices mailedJuly and August
Board of Equalization window45 days from the original mailing
Tax notices mailedBy November 1
Last day to pay without penaltyNovember 30
Taxes become delinquentDecember 1

A Utah home that serves as someone's primary residence is taxed on 55 percent of its market value, because of a 45 percent residential exemption. The state tax commission notes the exemption does not carry over automatically after a sale, so the new owner has to file. Applications go to the county Board of Equalization by September 15.

The county recorder at 2001 South State Street, Suite N1-600, takes deeds Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. It does not prepare documents or notarize them, and it does not decide whether a title is clear. Originals come back by mail two to three weeks after they are processed and imaged.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work for a Midvale seller?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Midvale follows the same recording path as any other sale, but it skips the buyer's loan, appraisal and repair negotiation. You tell us about the house, we review it and make an offer, and a title company handles the signing and recording at the county.

  • Houses with tenants, deferred repairs or inherited paperwork can be sold as they stand.
  • The closing date is set with you and the title company.
  • If the offer does not suit you, you can turn it down.

faqs.q: What is the population of Midvale, Utah?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau counted 36,028 people in Midvale in 2020, up 28.8 percent from 27,964 in 2010. The estimate shown at the top of this page is the more recent figure.

faqs.q: When are Midvale property taxes due?
faqs.a: The Salt Lake County calendar lists November 30 as the last day to pay current-year real property tax without penalty. Taxes become delinquent on December 1.

faqs.q: Is Midvale in Canyons School District?
faqs.a: Yes, Canyons School District is the main district for Midvale, which has four elementary schools, two middle schools and Hillcrest High School. Check the district's boundary lookup for a specific address.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent out a house in Midvale?
faqs.a: Yes, Midvale requires a landlord business license. The city says landlord licenses expire August 31 and are due no later than September 15.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Midvale house that has tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes. Many Midvale sellers are landlords, since the Census Bureau puts owner-occupancy at 43.4 percent. Share the lease and rent roll with the buyer early so the closing date can account for the lease terms.
